claims.text: The starting HfZrTiTa0.53 alloy has a quasi-static yield strength of approximately 786 MPa.
The starting HfZrTiTa0.53 alloy has a quasi-static compressive strength of approximately 1314 MPa.
The starting HfZrTiTa0.53 alloy has a quasi-static fracture strain of approximately 13.5%.
Approximately 10 at.% W can be introduced by partially substituting Ta in HfZrTiTa0.53.
The W substitution will produce a fine dispersion of W-rich precipitates in the primary matrix.
The modified alloy will have a dual-phase microstructure consisting of the original matrix and W-rich precipitates.
The W-rich precipitates will provide additional dislocation-storage sites and stronger barriers at precipitate/matrix interfaces.
Dislocations will bypass the proposed W-rich precipitates by Orowan looping.
Dislocation accumulation at precipitate/matrix interfaces will increase strain hardening.
Increased dislocation-storage capacity and strain hardening will delay adiabatic shear localization at high strain rates.
The W-modified alloy will have higher dynamic yield strength than the baseline alloy near 3000 s^-1.
The W-modified alloy will have higher dynamic compressive strength than the baseline alloy near 3000 s^-1.
The W-modified alloy will have a uniform or fracture strain greater than 13.5% near 3000 s^-1.
The W-modified alloy will deform more uniformly and resist adiabatic shear localization better than the baseline alloy.
The W-modified alloy will moderate impact-induced energy release.
The predictions apply at approximately 3000 s^-1, at room temperature, under dynamic adiabatic compression.
Rapid adiabatic heating near 3000 s^-1 typically causes poor strain hardening and localized failure.
A reported W10 HEA reaches an ultimate strength of 2300 MPa at 3000 s^-1.
A reported W10 HEA reaches strains of 20% and 24% at 2000 and 3000 s^-1, respectively.

contradictions.description: The predicted outcome is described relative to quasi-static baseline values, including the 13.5% fracture strain, whereas the matched experiment compares both alloys under dynamic loading. Thus the stated numerical comparator and the experimental control are not under the same loading regime.
